title: Stable softmax and scaled dot-product attention
goal:
Implement Equation 1 from Section 3.2.1: $\operatorname{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \operatorname{softmax}(QK^\top / \sqrt{d_k})\,V$.

Write two functions:

- `softmax(x, axis=-1)` returns a numerically stable softmax of `x` along `axis`. The output has the same shape as `x`.
- `scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V, mask=None)` returns `(output, weights)`. `Q` has shape `(..., n, d_k)`, `K` has shape `(..., m, d_k)`, and `V` has shape `(..., m, d_v)`. `output` has shape `(..., n, d_v)` and `weights` has shape `(..., n, m)`. The optional boolean `mask` broadcasts to `(..., n, m)`, and `True` means the query may attend to that key.
hints: Subtract the maximum along `axis` (with `keepdims=True`) before you call `np.exp`. The result doesn't change, and `exp(1000)` no longer overflows.
Use `np.swapaxes(K, -1, -2)` instead of `K.T`, so the same code handles batched and per-head inputs.
Divide the scores by `np.sqrt(d_k)`, where `d_k = Q.shape[-1]`. The width of `V` plays no part in the scale.
Replace masked scores with `-1e9` before the softmax. Zero is a valid score, so a zero keeps the key in play.
